title: Re: Saltline: First-person shooter built by Fable 5.2...
text:
I've been building an FPS since I realized Opus 4.8 claude had some essence of taste and modeling capability. I have 0 experience in game development. Along the way I learned how hard video game development really is and have a new respect for indie studios. AI will never replace original story telling and artwork - having a firm foundation and building the first models and level myself was key.

Since then, each model advancement has made it easier and easier to delegate and form workflows around each aspect of making my game - to the point that I login once and awhile to sculpt, get visual feedback for textures lighting and level design... I get a level done a week - test it myself, and ship it to beta testers who auto update and can send me anonymous feedback - all thanks to Opus.

I'm one dude - and I think this is a crippling vision to some of what's to come. AAA studios certainly know and will serve you AI generated games instead of paying talented people. I hope those talented people getting displaced can get enabled cause what I've done is pretty amazing.

title: Re: Work at the Frontier: AI's effect on freelance wor...
text:
It sounds like they're mainly saying that there are certain categories of work in which people use AI to handle things themselves (directly via ChatGPT) and other categories for which they still post a freelance listing (especially if it requires skills across multiple domains).

Writing, illustration, and tech support seem to be the categories people handle themselves most often via AI, according to the first graphic... But then the second graphic suggests that the number of freelance postings for a top 'do-it-yourself-with-AI' category like writing is only down about 0.5% year over year. That almost suggests there isn't really an effect. Even the largest-changing category in that graphic, web development, is down only about 2%.

I think I conceptually can agree with their implication that AI allows freelancers to take on more breadth on their own, but the data/graphics they're presenting are confusing me. I'm not sure I get it.

text:
When Anthropic released "claude design" people were telling that figma is dead now, but in fact claude design didn't move forward and stayed as a "fallback tool" when you quickly need to check / edit something. And for the serious work you still go to Figma and other designer tools. 
I have a feeling that Whiteboards, Sheets, Docs and so on will be the same - it's a nicer way to present artefacts, discuss them and maybe make notes, but for the proper editor experience you'll go to the tools which were designed for these things. And I'm not saying that Claude Something tools are bad, they're just overly simplified and limited, probably on purpose.

title: Show HN: Crewplane, you design and own the workflows, agents run them
text:
I built Crewplane because I wanted more control and flexibility over how my coding agents work together, and a way to trace what happened.

Workflow is defined in Markdown, and Crewplane runs the nodes defined in the workflow using native coding CLIs such as Codex and Claude Code. So the control is back to you: different workflows for different tasks with different models, what they depend on, and how they run (parallel or sequential or both). Every input, intermediate output, log, manifest, and final result is preserved on disk so you can trace a run after the fact.

Workflows can be reused and composed into larger pipelines, and interrupted workflows can be resumed. There is no vendor lock in, and it’s easy to adapt your workflows for various tasks - research, design, implementation, debugging, deployment, anything that works as structured procedures.

Give it a try and adapt your own workflows, there is a built-in Mock CLI so you can just try the workflow syntax and composition without worrying about costs (no model calls). Any feedback or suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

Open source (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/crewplaneai/crewplane

title: Show HN: Glitch/Distorion page transitions with HTML-in-Canvas
text:
Hey HN! I released VFX-JS Transitions, a WebGL page transition library built on HTML-in-Canvas API.

You can add GPU-powered page transitions to your website with just a few lines. It takes care of capturing the pages, holding the old one on screen, managing render passes and all sorts of other chores.

It comes with presets like glitch, datamosh and pixel sort, and you can also write your own transitions in GLSL. It ships a SKILL.md, so you can ask Claude etc to write the transition you want.

HTML-in-Canvas was released in Chrome 157, so you can use it today in your website. Other browsers don't support it yet, but I think HTML-in-Canvas is a real breakthrough for web design, and it's worth experimenting with today.

For other browsers, VFX-JS falls back to a DOM-to-SVG workaround. It can't capture everything, but you can start using it now!

docs: https://amagi.dev/vfx-js-transitions/ repo: https://github.com/fand/vfx-js

Any feedback is welcome! Thanks.
author: amagitakayosi

title: Show HN: Ramble – Message your agent directly from your Apple Watch
text:
I made Ramble because I wanted to get off my phone but still be able to capture thoughts, reminders, action items - whatever. Some of my best thoughts happen when I'm playing with my kids or on a run - and this lets me stay in the moment, fire off a quick message on my watch and not get pulled into the screen waiting for AI to respond - never get sucked into 'lets solve this now' mindset.

Ramble is designed for Apple Watch & offline first - to capture voice quickly and queue up messages to send when it can. The slim relay backend uses cloud transcription (Grok Whisper currently), then holds the message in an inbox for your agent to pickup and process, then gets purged from the backend after acknowledgement.

No accounts, no signups. It uses Apple's App Attest for endpoint security. It works great with current gen personal agents like Muse, GrokBot, etc. (GrokBot supports incoming webhooks so its instant. Muse doesn't, so it polls every couple minutes (without waking the agent)) The linking process is surprisingly easy.

Would love to hear what you think!
